title: Applied ML Evals Centralized Playbook: Onboarding, Prompt Sets, Quantization, and Regression Triage
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview

This playbook consolidates Redwood's recommended end-to-end process for bringing models into production through the eval harness. It covers: eval-harness onboarding, prompt set and benchmark standards, model onboarding checklists, quality guardrails and monitoring, quantization profile validation, and regression triage workflows. The goal is a reproducible, auditable path from prototype model to production deployment with clear ownership and SLOs for quality and cost.

Contents (quick links)
1. Principles and goals
2. Eval-harness onboarding checklist
3. Prompt sets & benchmark standards
4. Model onboarding guide
5. Quality guardrails and monitoring thresholds
6. Quantization profile validation & matrix
7. Regression triage playbook (incident-style workflow)
8. Roles & ownership
9. Templates & CLI examples
10. References and related pages

1. Principles and goals
- Reproducibility: every model candidate must have a deterministic eval run that can be replayed.
- Guardrails-first: automated checks (safety, hallucination, performance) run before manual review.
- Cost-aware: evaluate unit cost impact from quantization, batching, KV cache behavior.
- Fast triage: when regressions occur, reduce MTTR with clear triage steps and telemetry.

SLOs (applied-ml team)
- Pre-prod eval coverage: >= 90% of model changes must pass the eval suite before rollout.
- Regression detection: critical regressions detected within 24 hours of deployment with automated alerts.
- Triage MTTR: median time-to-resolution for high-severity regressions <= 48 hours.

2. Eval-harness onboarding checklist (step-by-step)
1) Create a new eval job in the eval-harness repo following the naming convention: eval-<model>-<task>-<date>. Example: eval-llama2-chat-summarization-2026-09-15.
2) Add canonical prompt set(s) (see section 3) and attach metadata: domain, language, difficulty, expected output type.
3) Provide a baseline: reference model and baseline metrics (accuracy/ROUGE/BLEU/embedding-similarity).
4) Define pass/fail thresholds and regression gates in the job config.
5) Commit a CI trigger that runs the eval on PRs that modify model-serving code or prompts.
6) Attach ownership and reviewer(s) in metadata.
7) Run and record the first full eval, upload results to the eval dashboard, and link to PR.

Minimum eval job config (example YAML excerpt)
| key | example value | notes |
|-----|---------------|-------|
| name | eval-<model>-<task> | 1-2 words task name |
| baseline_model | model-v1 | used for regression comparison |
| datasets | promptset-id, coverage-suite | comma-separated |
| thresholds | accuracy:0.82, hallucination:0.01 | pass/fail gates |
| owners | aisha.patel@redwood.ai | at least one owner |

3. Prompt sets & benchmark standards
Prompt set taxonomy
- Canonical prompt sets: curated, reviewed sets for each task domain (customer-visible behaviors). Used for gating and long-term quality metrics.
- Stress tests: adversarial or edge-case prompts intended to detect brittle failure modes.
- Coverage suites: stratified prompts across languages, lengths, and intents to surface distributional issues.

Prompt set metadata (required fields)
- id: unique id (promptset-<area>-<ver>)
- domain: e.g., "summarization", "code-generation", "customer-support"
- languages: list of languages covered
- split: canonical|stress|coverage
- owner: team or person

Benchmarking guidance
- Use stable seeds for sampling.
- Report metrics by slice (length, language, style) and overall.
- For generation tasks: report ROUGE, BERTScore, BLEU where applicable plus downstream task success (if available).
- For chat/assistant tasks: include human-eval summaries (at least 50 samples for critical features) and automated safety checks.

4. Model onboarding guide
Pre-onboarding (research)
- Internal review: short PRD describing intended improvements, expected cost delta, and risk assessment.
- Smoke tests: local inference sanity checks and tokenization compatibility.

Onboarding steps
1) Create model card draft with architecture, training data summary, license, expected latency/cost, and known limitations.
2) Run full eval-harness suite: canonical prompt sets + coverage + stress.
3) Populate quantization profile matrix (section 6).
4) Perform end-to-end integration test with serving runtime: KV cache warmup, batching scenarios, streaming.
5) Security & privacy review if model or prompts reference customer data.
6) Canary rollout plan with rollback criteria and monitoring thresholds.

Model-card minimum fields
- model_id, version, license, training_data_summary, intended_use, known_limitations, owner, contact.

5. Quality guardrails and monitoring thresholds
Automated guardrails (run on every eval and in-prod monitoring):
- Hallucination rate threshold: < 1% on canonical factual-check prompts for knowledge-base tasks.
- Toxicity/safety: use safety classifier; block if safety-score > 0.7 (per task calibration).
- Blank or truncated responses: < 0.5% in production traces.
- Latency regression: P95 latency increase <= 20% vs baseline.
- Cost regression: per-token cost increase <= 15% unless approved.

Monitoring dashboards (recommended panels)
- Eval vs baseline: key metrics and delta-by-slice.
- Real traffic quality: sampled human eval summaries, top error buckets.
- Model variant routing and fallback rates.
- Quantization impact: token throughput and quality delta.

6. Quantization profile validation & matrix
Purpose: codify how candidate quantization schemes affect quality, latency, and cost.

Quantization matrix (example columns)
- profile_id | dtype | per-token latency delta | accuracy delta | cost delta | recommended_use_case
- qfp8-int8-4bit | int4 | -30% | -1.1% | -45% | latency-sensitive low-cost chat
- qfp16-8bit | int8 | -18% | -0.2% | -30% | general purpose production

Validation steps
1) Run quantized model through canonical prompt sets and stress tests.
2) Record slice-wise metrics and identify any >1% absolute drops on critical slices.
3) Validate end-to-end latency in serving runtime under expected batching.
4) Evaluate numeric stability on long-context scenarios (KV cache correctness).
5) If regressions found, test mixed-mode (quantize attention/query projections but keep FFN in FP16).

Acceptance criteria for shipping a quantized variant
- No critical-slice accuracy degradation > 1.5% absolute.
- Hallucination and safety metrics within pre-approved tolerances.
- Throughput gains must justify rollback risk (cost savings > 20% or latency improvement > 15%).

7. Regression triage playbook (incident-style workflow)
Severity definitions
- Sev 1 (Critical): Major production regression impacting multiple customers or breakage of core functionality.
- Sev 2 (High): Noticeable quality drop for a feature group or significant latency/cost regression for a single product.
- Sev 3 (Medium): Localized or minor regressions detected by evals or small customer impact.

Triage steps (for any detected regression)
1) Automated alert triggers: eval or observability indicates threshold breach -> create triage ticket and notify on #applied-ml-triage.
2) Initial assessment (owner within 1 hour): determine if regression is real by comparing to stored baseline artifacts (eval outputs, hashes).
3) Narrow down vector: prompts, model variant, quantization profile, runtime change, routing policy. Use the checklist below.
4) Remediation plan: rollback to baseline variant OR patch model/config and run focused evals.
5) Postmortem: within 5 business days for Sev 1/2, document root cause, timeline, and preventive actions.

Triage checklist (quick reproducibility)
- Re-run failing eval job with same seed and environment.
- Confirm model binary checksum vs stored artifact.
- Check recent infra changes (kernel/driver updates, serving runtime release).
- Verify prompt set integrity and tokenization changes.
- Validate quantization profile used in production matches test profile.

8. Roles & ownership
- Model Owner (applied-ml): responsible for eval design, thresholds, and remediation.
- Platform Owner (eng-serving-runtime): responsible for runtime regressions, kernel changes, and latency/cost SLOs.
- QA / Eval Reviewer: signs off on human-eval summaries and stress tests.
- Security/Privacy: reviews model cards and monitors data handling.

9. Templates & CLI examples
Create an eval job (CLI example)
```
# from eval-harness repository
rw-eval create --name eval-llama2-summarization --model model-llama2-v2 --promptset promptset-summarization-v1 --baseline model-llama2-v1 --thresholds '{"rouge":0.45,"hallucination":0.01}' --owner aisha.patel@redwood.ai
```
Quick re-run for triage
```
rw-eval run --job eval-llama2-summarization-2026-09-15 --seed 42 --env staging --output artifacts/eval-llama2-summarization-2026-09-15.json
```
Example model-card snippet (JSON-like plaintext)
```
model_id: model-llama2-v2
version: v2.0
license: apache-2.0
training_data_summary: 'Mixture of web, books, code up to 2025-12'
intended_use: 'general-language, chat assistant, summarization'
known_limitations: 'degraded factuality on long-horizon knowledge queries (see section X)'
owner: applied-ml@redwood.ai
```

Appendix: Useful queries and dashboards
- Query: rolling 7-day hallucination rate per model: SELECT model_id, date, avg(hallucination_rate) FROM eval_metrics WHERE date > now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY model_id, date;
- Dashboard panels to clone: eval-vs-baseline (by slice), quantization-impact panel, production-human-eval-sample stream.
